name: trigonometry
title: Trigonometry
scope: This card solves right and oblique triangle questions from the sides and angles already given.
method: Decide from the given data whether the triangle is right or oblique.
Use opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse only for a right triangle and a named acute angle.
Use SOHCAHTOA or a^2+b^2=c^2 only when a right angle is given.
Otherwise pair each side with its opposite angle in the law of sines or the law of cosines.
For three side lengths, set P = a+b+c and s = P/2, then apply Heron's formula.
If a side or angle is missing, name it; do not invent a length.

formulas.name: SOHCAHTOA
formulas.expr: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent
formulas.use: In a right triangle these ratios relate one acute angle to two sides.

formulas.name: Pythagorean theorem
formulas.use: In a right triangle, c is the hypotenuse and a and b are the legs.

formulas.name: Perimeter
formulas.use: The perimeter is the sum of the three side lengths.

formulas.name: Heron's formula
formulas.use: three side lengths give the area; the perimeter is the sum of the sides; do not treat the word surface as Earth's surface.

formulas.name: Law of cosines
formulas.use: Relates the three sides to angle C, the angle opposite side c.

formulas.name: Law of sines
formulas.expr: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
formulas.use: Pairs each side with the sine of its opposite angle.

checks: The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle.
The law of sines pairs each side with its opposite angle.
The law of cosines uses angle C opposite side c.
Heron needs three side lengths; s is half the perimeter, not a new measurement.
limits: SOHCAHTOA and the Pythagorean theorem apply to right triangles only.
The SSA case can have zero, one, or two triangles; do not pick one without a reason.
This card does not supply a side or angle the user did not give.
